chapter: Chicago, the Marable boats and Marge's St. Louis family band
title: The six-piece band and the name Jazz-O-Maniacs
summary: At 19 Marge played in Charlie's six-piece band; as jazz came in he named it Charlie Creath and his Jazz-O-Maniacs.

story.theme_name: First paying gigs: getting started as a young professional
story.community_name: First paid gigs: pay, bands and young beginnings

blocks.x: 18, 19, because I had been out of high school. Still not 20 because I'd been out of high school hanging around there, didn't know what I wanted to do. But I didn't want to go to college, I know that. I didn't want -- not that I didn't love school and all, but my mother had to work too hard. So my first job was playing with the band, which was just about six pieces; trombone, saxophone, trumpet, piano, drums and guitar. That was the instrumentation. And boy they played like mad, and then finally the band got so good everybody loved it, so Charlie wanted a name for it. What are we going to name it. So we rehearsed -- and the boys were happy with me, they said I played good. The most they wanted was accompaniment, they didn't care whether it was a lot of executions, as long as I played the right notes and the right tempo.
And then Charlie said jazz was coming in and jazz --
Well, what sort of music were you playing then before, sort of dance music, popular?
No, you say jazz was coming in.

Well, we didn't call it jazz. It was jazz but they didn't call it -- they called it jazz. Then we started to call it jazz and Charlie said now they have a name for the band. And finally he came up with the name Jazz O'maniacs. That was the name of our band.
Charlie Cramp and his Jazz O'Maniacs.
